investigation.title: Swarm Gateway 502 Blocking All Remote Agent Checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime)
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents feature checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-08-24T04:45–04:46Z with an identical 502 bad_gateway error: the production API could not reach the swarm ELB endpoint at POST /v1/agents. Because the failure is shared across every sibling check and no evidence was collected (all four required fields—orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState—are missing), the fault is localized to the swarm gateway layer upstream of agent provisioning, not to any individual check's logic.
investigation.rootCause: The swarm gateway (an AWS ELB in us-east-2 fronting /v1/agents) was unreachable from the production API at the time of the eval run. Every POST /api/agents request made by the eval runner was rejected with HTTP 502 and error code bad_gateway before any agent could be provisioned, preventing all required evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) from being collected. This is an eval-observed infrastructure connectivity failure localized to the swarm gateway dependency; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence to confirm a broader production outage.

investigation.title: image-generation-stream Eval Failure: OpenAI API Credit Balance Exhausted
investigation.summary: The image-generation-stream eval failed because the OpenAI API key configured for the eval environment has no remaining credits, causing the /api/generate/image/stream endpoint to return a credit_balance_exhausted error. The stream terminated with a generation_error frame instead of the required generation_completed frame, so both contract assertions (frameTypes contains "generation_completed" and imageUrlPresent equals true) were violated.
investigation.rootCause: The OpenAI organization account associated with the API key used by the eval runner has exhausted its credit balance. When the runner called /api/generate/image/stream, the upstream OpenAI API rejected the request with error code "credit_balance_exhausted" and type "insufficient_quota". The server translated this into a generation_error SSE frame with code GENERATION_FAILED, which terminated the stream before any generation_completed frame or image artifact URL could be produced. This is an external billing/quota condition, not a code defect in the eval runner or the image generation route itself. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the evidence; this is an eval infrastructure failure scoped to the eval environment's OpenAI credentials.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Provisioning: Swarm Gateway 502 Blocking All Remote-Agent Checks
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-08-24T04:45–04:46Z with an identical 502 bad-gateway error indicating the swarm gateway ELB at /v1/agents was unreachable during agent provisioning. Because agent creation is the first step in the remote-agent-runtime probe (run-status-probes.mjs line 1918: createAgent), the gateway failure prevented any evidence from being collected, causing the expected-output contract to be entirely unmet.
investigations.rootCause: The swarm gateway (an AWS ELB in us-east-2 fronting /v1/agents) was unreachable at the time of the eval run. Every remote-agent check that calls POST /api/agents received HTTP 502 with error code bad_gateway and the message "swarm gateway unreachable during agent provisioning." Because remote-agent-runtime depends on a successful createAgent call before it can exercise the runtime, the gateway failure is the single upstream dependency whose outage caused all three sibling checks to fail with the same error message. This is an eval-observed infrastructure failure; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so impact to production users cannot be confirmed from this packet alone.

possibleCauses: Primary: The AWS ELB serving the swarm gateway at /v1/agents in us-east-2 was down, misconfigured, or had no healthy targets at the time of the eval run, causing the production-api to return 502 bad_gateway for all POST /api/agents requests.

Secondary: A network routing or security-group change between the production-api and the swarm ELB blocked outbound connections to the ELB endpoint, producing connection errors that the API surfaced as 502.
Tertiary: The swarm service behind the ELB was restarting or had crashed, leaving the ELB with zero healthy instances and returning 502 for all incoming requests.

Lower probability: A transient DNS or TLS misconfiguration on the ELB endpoint caused the production-api to fail to establish a connection, resulting in the observed 'error sending request for url' message.
